speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please tell me, how many weeks pregnant are you, and when did you first notice the vaginal bleeding and abdominal pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old woman, gravida 2, para 1, at 38 weeks' gestation. The patient reports experiencing vaginal bleeding for the past hour accompanied by severe abdominal pain. She mentions that she felt contractions before the onset of the bleeding, but the contractions ceased once the bleeding began. Her first childbirth was a cesarean section due to nonreassuring fetal heart rate.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Given your history of a prior cesarean section and the sudden onset of severe pain with bleeding at 38 weeks, is there any possibility you have passed a clot or are experiencing vaginal discharge? Also, have you felt a gush of fluid, or is your abdominal pain localized to the uterus?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Vaginal bleeding. I also have Severe abdominal pain, History of contractions that stopped, Previous cesarean delivery. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Gastroenteritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Uterine Rupture
REQUEST IMAGES: Ultrasound_pelvis_with_doppler
REQUEST TEST: Fetal heart rate monitoring and complete blood count.

The symptoms you are describing, especially the cessation of contractions followed by sudden severe pain and bleeding in the setting of a prior C-section, are highly concerning for uterine rupture, not gastroenteritis. We need to confirm the status of the fetus and the integrity of the uterus immediately.
